angle: Why an open connector standard matters for plugging AI into enterprise systems
sourceTitle: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
linkedinPost:
What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP), in plain English?

Definition: MCP is an open standard that lets AI apps plug into external systems through a shared connector. Think of it like a universal power adapter for tools, not a magic brain upgrade.

Analogy: It’s the corporate USB port for AI — same plug, different devices.

How it works / value:
- Common interface: One way to connect to data sources, tools, and workflows.
- Safer patterns: It centralizes permissions, but doesn’t guarantee safe actions.
- Faster integration: Build once, reuse across apps to cut integration toil.

Hypothetical: A support assistant uses MCP to fetch order status from ERP, open a ticket in Zendesk, and trigger a refund workflow — all via standard connectors.

Limitation: MCP doesn’t decide who can do what; your permission model and testing do. A bad connector still does bad things, just more consistently.

My take: Standards speed value when paired with clear guardrails and owner teams. Who owns your connectors — platform, security, or the app squads?

#EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption
